DisplayName: .NET quality repair with diagnosis and bounded bughunt
Summary: Reusable .NET repair subprocess that separates evidence diagnosis, typed product or proof correction, independent validation, specialist bughunt, bounded re-repair, and accepted or no-go handoff.
ValueStatement: Repairs concrete .NET product or proof-contract defects without blind retries, manufactured source edits, or implementer self-acceptance.
InterfaceContractSummary: The parent supplies QA findings, implementation evidence, product context, and failed proof; the child returns independently accepted repair evidence or an explicit no-go packet.
GovernanceNotes: Diagnosis, mutation, and acceptance remain separate responsibilities. A known failed validation result is an unresolved defect, not residual risk.
ChangeSummary: Adds progress-sensitive manager and specialist assistance to .NET quality repair.
GovernancePolicySummary: One diagnosis-guided repair and one specialist-guided re-repair are allowed before no-go handoff.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: Product-repair branches require mutation evidence, proof-only branches require corrected current-execution proof, and neither action may accept itself.
OperatingModeSummary: Guarded autonomous execution with manager diagnosis and independent QA branch decisions.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Exercises deterministic repair, browser-capable validation, specialist handoff, and bounded no-go behavior.
Metrics: Repair acceptance rate after manager diagnosis.
Share of persistent defects resolved by specialist bughunt.
Number of no-go outcomes with exact current-execution failure evidence.
Risks: Diagnosis targets symptoms instead of the concrete failed invariant.
QA accepts known failed proof as residual risk.
TailoringRules: Use build and test proof for every .NET target and runtime/browser proof only when the failed behavior or product contract is UI-visible.
Keep the repair inside the approved product boundary and preserve accepted upstream behavior.
Use the no-go path after the specialist-guided second repair still fails; do not loop back again inside this subprocess.

Steps.Title: Diagnose the exact quality failure
Steps.Subtitle: Specialist evidence triage before mutation
Steps.Notes: Begin with every exact ref listed under AgentFramework inherited parent-step artifact refs and read the relevant parent artifacts before diagnosis. Runtime-appended gate findings in those artifacts are authoritative even when the original agent summary claimed acceptance. A missing accepted implementation handoff is a symptom, not a standalone proof-only diagnosis: trace why the child withheld acceptance back to the authoritative criteria and actual product. Then inspect the referenced command receipts, browser snapshot, console log, screenshots, and implementation evidence that actually exist. Before completing, read representative current product source under the grounded product root at the most likely owning boundary; project files, bootstrap, router/app shell, imports, navigation, stylesheets, and upstream prose alone are not behavior-owning inspection unless the failed criterion is specifically owned there. For a visible UI error, compare rendered state, console diagnostics, styling, and the owning source before assuming which layer caused it. Name the exact failed invariant, correlate it to concrete source when evidence permits, identify the owning source/composition boundary, and define the smallest proof that must turn green. Do not edit product files. A visible error, failed command, broken formula, invalid output, or absent core workflow after repair is an unresolved product defect, not residual risk or an evidence-only handoff gap.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Parent QA disposition, exact failed proof, reviewed implementation evidence, product root, and inherited authoritative scope; diagnosis must not reduce the full core workflow to the latest proof gap.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Grounded defect diagnosis with owning boundary, repair target, exclusions, and proof plan.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Exact failing receipt or artifact refs, observed error, reproduction state, source hypothesis, and targeted validation plan.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Bughunt specialist owns the grounded root-cause diagnosis; the repair manager reviews the repair target but neither role can mutate product code or waive failed proof.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block only when the parent supplied no actionable failure evidence, product context is unavailable, or required evidence access is denied.

InstructionFragments.Title: Owning product source proof
InstructionFragments.Content: Before writing the diagnosis artifact or finalizing, inspect the grounded external product target, choose a behavior-owning source file for the observed failure, and call workspace_read_file on that exact external-target path in this execution. A directory listing, project/bootstrap/shell file, managed artifact, or upstream prose does not satisfy this obligation unless it directly owns the failed criterion. If the listed root has only directories, descend into the relevant product directory and read a concrete source file before concluding.

RequiredReceipts.Reason: The diagnosis must be grounded in a current-run owning product source read under the declared external product target.

Steps.Title: Apply the diagnosis-guided repair or proof correction
Steps.Subtitle: Typed product-mutation or proof-only action
Steps.Notes: Use the manager diagnosis as the repair contract and read the diagnosed current product source before choosing an action. If an expected control, state transition, interaction, visible surface, or runtime behavior is missing or broken, implement the smallest owning source change, read changed files back, run focused proof, and select product-repair-applied even when build/tests pass. For a visible UI failure without a matching console exception, inspect the rendered state, loaded styling, and owning source boundary before assuming an application exception. Select proof-only-revalidation-prepared only when the expected behavior already exists and works and the prior route, selector, or proof recipe was wrong. Independent QA still owns acceptance.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Grounded quality-failure diagnosis, parent implementation evidence, and approved product boundary.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Diagnosis-linked product repair or corrected proof plan with a typed action branch.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Selected action branch; changed files, readback, and mutation receipts for product repair, or current validation/runtime/browser evidence for proof-only correction.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Repair engineer selects and executes the diagnosis-supported action but cannot accept the final repair.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Return Blocked only for unavailable product root, denied mutation/validation tools, contradictory diagnosis, or required scope outside the approved boundary.

Steps.Title: Independently validate the repaired product
Steps.Subtitle: Accept or hand exact evidence to bughunt
Steps.Notes: Reproduce the original failed proof from the diagnosis and run the current .NET restore/build/test chain. When ProductAcceptanceCriteriaContract is present, only criteria with kind=ProductAcceptance and required=true gate the repair result. Preserve kind=DeliveryPlanning items as nonblocking context; they cannot select bughunt-required, block acceptance, or require human confirmation without a separate typed decision gate. For a UI-visible failure or UI product contract, launch the app, exercise the affected workflow, capture current-run snapshot/screenshot/console evidence, and stop the same runtime. A deterministic test through the typed storage adapter or coordinator is sufficient to prove graceful unavailable behavior unless a required ProductAcceptance criterion explicitly demands a live browser outage. For normal IndexedDB reload proof, use browser_evaluate to seed and inspect the declared schema, reload, and verify restored UI state without waiting for a workflow-generated nonzero value. Pass full managed filenames under artifacts/process-runs/<current-process-run-id>/browser/... to every browser evidence capture. If a bare provider-native screenshot is unreadable by workspace image analysis, recapture once with the full managed filename and retry before choosing repair, Blocked, or escalation. When a visual target exists, call workspace_analyze_images with source target first and delivered current-run screenshot second. Capture all proof before writing the primary artifact, then write it once with the final disposition; never create a provisional or placeholder Status: Blocked artifact. Known failed proof is not residual risk: if the original error persists, a new release-blocking error appears, an interaction produces no meaningful state change, or expected behavior is still broken, complete the step with bughunt-required and attach exact evidence. Select quality-repair-accepted only when current-execution proof is clean. Return Blocked only when required product access or validation capability was unavailable and no proof decision could be executed.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Inherited authoritative scope, original diagnosis, typed repair action, implementer receipts, and product validation contract with a literal current-execution receipt checklist.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Independent current-execution validation with accepted or bughunt-required disposition.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Restore/build/test receipts, exact original-proof reproduction, runtime/browser lifecycle proof when applicable, changed behavior, and clean or failing evidence.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Quality reviewer owns acceptance and cannot mutate product code or waive a known failure.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Return Blocked only when a required validation tool, product root, permission, or process contract is unavailable; use bughunt-required for an executed proof that still fails.

Steps.Title: Bughunt the persistent failure
Steps.Subtitle: Specialist comparison before second mutation
Steps.Notes: Compare the original diagnosis, first change set, and exact failed revalidation evidence. Before completing, read representative current product source under the grounded product root at the likely owning boundary; upstream prose is not product inspection. Inspect the concrete error and owning source/composition boundary, explain why the first repair did not resolve it or what it broke, and propose one precise second repair plus proof. For a visible UI error, compare rendered state, console diagnostics, styling, and the owning source before assuming which layer caused it. Do not edit product files and do not repeat the first plan unchanged. State the primary failure signature, owning boundary, rejected competing hypothesis, smallest different repair, and validation recipe that can falsify the second repair.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Inherited authoritative scope, original diagnosis, first repair change set, and exact bughunt-required validation evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Specialist root-cause delta and bounded second-repair plan.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Before/after failure comparison, overlooked cause or regression, owning source boundary, and targeted proof.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Bughunt specialist owns diagnosis but cannot mutate or accept the product.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block only when exact failed evidence or product source access is unavailable; do not issue the same plan without explaining the missed cause.

Steps.Title: Apply the specialist-guided repair or proof correction
Steps.Subtitle: One bounded typed second action
Steps.Notes: Apply the bughunt diagnosis to the exact owning boundary and read the diagnosed current product source before choosing an action. A missing expected control, state transition, interaction, visible surface, or real runtime error is a product defect even when build/tests pass: mutate the smallest owning source or configuration surface, read it back, run focused proof, state the delta from the first repair, and select product-repair-applied. For a visible UI failure without a matching console exception, inspect rendered state, loaded styling, and the owning source boundary before assuming an application exception. Select proof-only-revalidation-prepared only when the expected behavior already exists and works and the prior target, selector, or proof recipe was wrong. This is the final bounded repair action inside the subprocess.

Steps.OutputContractSummary: Specialist-guided product repair or corrected proof plan with a typed action branch.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Selected action branch and difference from the first action; mutation/readback evidence for product repair or current validation/runtime/browser evidence for proof-only correction.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Repair engineer owns the bounded second action but cannot accept it.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Return Blocked only for unavailable product root, denied tools, contradictory specialist plan, or required scope outside the approved boundary.

Steps.Title: Independently revalidate after bughunt
Steps.Subtitle: Final accepted or no-go decision
Steps.Notes: Reproduce the original and persistent failed proof, then run current restore/build/test and conditional runtime/browser validation. When ProductAcceptanceCriteriaContract is present, only criteria with kind=ProductAcceptance and required=true gate the repair result. Preserve kind=DeliveryPlanning items as nonblocking context; they cannot select quality-repair-no-go, block acceptance, or require human confirmation without a separate typed decision gate. A deterministic test through the typed storage adapter or coordinator is sufficient to prove graceful unavailable behavior unless a required ProductAcceptance criterion explicitly demands a live browser outage. For normal IndexedDB reload proof, use browser_evaluate to seed and inspect the declared schema, reload, and verify restored UI state without waiting for a workflow-generated nonzero value. Pass full managed filenames under artifacts/process-runs/<current-process-run-id>/browser/... to every browser evidence capture. If a bare provider-native screenshot is unreadable by workspace image analysis, recapture once with the full managed filename and retry before choosing no-go, Blocked, or escalation. When a visual target exists, call workspace_analyze_images with source target first and delivered current-run screenshot second. Capture all proof before writing the primary artifact and write it once with the final branch; never create a provisional Status: Blocked artifact. Select quality-repair-accepted only when both failure sets are resolved and no new release blocker exists. Known failed proof is not residual risk. Complete with quality-repair-no-go and exact failing evidence when the defect persists, an interaction remains unchanged, or the second repair introduces another release blocker; negative proof is not a Blocked outcome.

Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Return Blocked only for unavailable validation capability or product context; use quality-repair-no-go for executed proof that remains failed.
